rag-pipeline.prompt: Order the stages from ingestion to a grounded, cited answer.
rag-pipeline.steps[0].label: Ingest Trusted Source Documents
rag-pipeline.steps[0].detail: Retrieval can only ever surface what was ingested. Source selection is a governance decision, not a plumbing one.
rag-pipeline.steps[1].label: Clean, Split, and Attach Metadata
rag-pipeline.steps[1].detail: Chunking decides what a retrievable unit is; metadata is what later makes filtering and attribution possible.
rag-pipeline.steps[2].label: Create Embeddings for Each Chunk
rag-pipeline.steps[2].detail: Text becomes vectors. The embedding model chosen here constrains everything the retriever can distinguish.
rag-pipeline.steps[3].label: Store Chunks and Vectors in an Index
rag-pipeline.steps[3].detail: The index makes similarity search tractable. Access controls belong here, not only at the answer.
rag-pipeline.steps[4].label: Embed and Interpret the User Query
rag-pipeline.steps[4].detail: The query is embedded by the same model as the chunks, or the two live in incomparable spaces.
rag-pipeline.steps[5].label: Retrieve, Filter, and Rerank Evidence
rag-pipeline.steps[5].detail: Recall decides whether the right passage is available at all; ranking decides whether it survives the context budget.
rag-pipeline.steps[6].label: Build a Prompt with Evidence and Instructions
rag-pipeline.steps[6].detail: The retrieved evidence is placed in the prompt with instructions on how to use it and when to refuse.
rag-pipeline.steps[7].label: Generate, Validate, and Cite the Grounded Answer
rag-pipeline.steps[7].detail: The model answers from the supplied evidence and cites it, so a reader can check rather than trust.
